retrofit: logic-gates-cmos activity-factor note said some books 'add a factor of ½ instead'; now states that books counting every transition (rising and falling) write ½ × α × C × V^2 × f with an α twice as large, giving the same power, and gives α ≈ 0.1 for data / α = 1 for a clock (Harris lect7; Wikipedia CMOS).
retrofit: logic-gates-cmos 'The V² term makes voltage reduction powerful ..., and why phones scale...' was ungrammatical; split into a separate sentence.
retrofit: logic-adders-alu barrel-shifter prose used undefined 'log2(n)'; now 'a tree of muxes whose depth is the base-2 logarithm of the width: 6 levels for 64 bits'.

retrofit: logic-datapath-memory single-cycle block's where lines gave no values; each delay now carries its illustrative value (250/150/200/250/50 ps) and the lead-in labels them as illustrative, not measured.
retrofit: logic-boolean-algebra q6 worked example lines 'A + A′·B = 1 + 0 = 1 + B' / '0 + B = 0 + B' did not say which A they assume; now annotated 'for A = 1' / 'for A = 0'.

retrofit: glossary espresso said it is 'from the University of California, Berkeley'; ESPRESSO was first developed at IBM by Brayton et al. (1982), with ESPRESSO-MV by Rudell at Berkeley (1986); definition corrected.
retrofit: glossary propagation-delay reintroduced a universal 'picoseconds to tens of picoseconds' figure that the lesson deliberately omits (evidence gap); removed.

retrofit: glossary sources that did not resolve or pointed at the wrong page fixed: Two-level_logic (missing) -> Logic_optimization; Transistor_sizing (missing) -> Logical_effort; Floating_ground (different concept) -> Pull-up_resistor; Handshaking (redirects to the greeting) -> Handshake_(computing); Logic_level for logic depth (voltage levels) -> Propagation_delay; Subtraction#Borrowing (dead anchor) -> Carry_flag; Monotonic_function#Monotone_Boolean_functions -> #In_Boolean_functions; Race_condition#Electronics -> #In_electronics; time-borrowing -> Harris CMOS VLSI lecture 11; lut -> AMD UG474; DVFS -> Voltage_and_frequency_scaling.

retrofit: glossary aliases that captured other senses removed or narrowed: 'carry'/'carries'/'carry in' (verb 'carries the sign', 'a link can carry in one frame'), 'lw'/'sw' (matched 'readelf -lW'; now 'load word'/'store word'), 'pipeline' and 'pipeline stages' (FPGA/switch pipelines; Arch 04 owns it), 'Arm' (case-insensitive 'arm'), 'BL' (shadowed Arch 03 branch-with-link), 'lookup table(s)' (shadowed Arch 03 software lookup table and fell back to DSA/system-design), 'fanout' (B-tree fanout in Arch 05), 'supply voltage', 'logic levels', 'load capacitance', 'regeneration', 'two-level', 'to ground'/'connected to ground' (56 synth hits), 'delay buffers' (synth audio), 'distributes over', 'wraps round'/'wrap round'/'wrapping round' (integer wrap-around elsewhere), "don't care", 'critical paths', 'condition flags', 'signed overflow' (C UB elsewhere), 'a borrow' (Rust), 'feedback loop', 'rising/falling/positive edge' ('positive edge weights' in DSA), 'clock rate', 'race-free', 'single-cycle' (synth waveforms), 'out-of-order', 'always blocks' (verb), 'in series', 'AND term(s)' ('index and term').

retrofit: glossary terms whose own names fell back with a wrong sense renamed to scoped forms: 'AND gate'/'OR gate'/'NOT gate' -> 'AND (logic)'/'OR (logic)'/'NOT (logic)' with exact-case aliases AND/OR/NOT ('and gate E2E', 'qubits and gates'); 'Identity law' -> 'Identity law (Boolean)' (monad identity law); 'Product term' -> 'Product term (Boolean)'; 'Status flags' -> 'Status flags (ALU)' (file status flags); 'Setup time'/'Hold time' -> '(flip-flop)' (connection setup, lock hold time); 'Clock skew' -> 'Clock skew (on-chip)'; 'Row buffer' -> 'Row buffer (DRAM)' with lesson now saying 'DRAM row buffer'.
retrofit: glossary fan-out, fan-in and finite-state machine definitions generalised so their cross-subject links (system-design fan-out, goroutine fan-in, TCP/software state machines) are correct.

retrofit: glossary input-capacitance definition now distinguishes it from total load capacitance; dynamic-power 'the most effective saving' hedged to 'often the most effective single saving'; SystemVerilog 'the main language' -> 'widely used' (IEEE 1800); VHDL now cites IEEE 1076 and 1980s VHSIC origin.

retrofit: logic-karnaugh-maps bold 'wraps round' -> 'wrap-round adjacency' so it links without the removed ordinary-phrase aliases; leading-space and missing-blank-line formatting after formula blocks fixed in gates, adders, sequential and datapath lessons.

revisions.scope: final cross-module/cross-subject reconciliation: Off-by-one phrase "2 multiplied by itself k times" replaced with "k copies of 2 multiplied together": 10 replacements across logic-boolean-algebra, logic-karnaugh-maps, logic-adders-alu, logic-datapath-memory. logic-adders-alu: "status flags" reworded to "condition flags" (still links status-flag after its plural alias was removed).

summary.counting: Overlapping review groups: one per active lesson, formula card, question and glossary entry; not a count of atomic facts.

corrections: Fixed the lesson and original subtraction question: retained four-bit arithmetic is reduced modulo sixteen; an unreduced eighteen is no longer equated with two, nor fifteen with negative one.
Fixed three adder cards whose plus sign was wrongly defined as Boolean OR; their operands now use ordinary binary addition.
Bracketed both quiz timing substitutions before the picosecond unit, keeping the full arithmetic sum within that unit.

Replaced 113 generic formula-card readings with readings of the actual expression or proposed identity. Repaired sentences, bullet emphasis and punctuation split around mathematical cards; removed mathematical multi-bit products disguised as inline code.

Clarified Brent–Kung counting: eleven scheduled rows in the original buffered sixty-four-bit layout include forwarding; the longest unbuffered path contains ten combining cells. Independently checked the graph.

Qualified same-phase latch versus flip-flop shifting, asynchronous-reset deassertion, synchroniser reliability and statement-specific non-blocking scheduling; no fixed MTBF or universal hardware guarantee is implied.
Corrected a maxterm distractor label to row one while retaining the original answer key; the expression is still a distractor for the minterm question.
Clarified that unused instruction encodings are not automatically allowed don’t-cares: required illegal-instruction behaviour must still be implemented.

Corrected inherited dictionary meanings for active-low assertion, active-high decoder assumptions, general latches, combinational settling, feedback, hardware counters, programme-counter instruction address and finite-width two’s-complement negation.

Narrowed ordinary consensus and latch-transparent/opaque aliases; open-drain now reuses the existing output definition rather than opening wired-OR wiring. Added a precise open-collector output entry.

Qualified activity factors, capacitive versus other dynamic power, drive strength, multiported-register costs, row-buffer latency, FPGA configuration, VHDL/Verilog event sensitivity and topology assumptions.

Used the independently fetched original Shannon paper’s confirmed 1938 publication date rather than repeating an uncorroborated exact thesis year; retained the switching-circuit connection. Boole’s publication dates and Karnaugh’s 1953 Bell Labs attribution were independently corroborated.
Corrected RISC-V source labels that claimed to be MIT notes; added directly relevant primary Boole, Karnaugh and BOOM references.

Coordinated with the different Data Representation verifier to broaden the earlier-owned winning register definition and prevent hardware-register phrases from opening a device-controller status-register entry.

glossaryReview.note: No claim of fresh full factual verification of the unchanged glossary; earlier confidence and term hashes are retained.

logic-binary-values.rationale: Operation notation and precedence remain essential because later circuits use the symbols; the redundant row-count equation is removed. Voltage abstractions remain visible and the question now tests completeness of a specification.

questionsRewritten.logic-binary-values-q1: Replace row-count arithmetic with completeness reasoning.

logic-xor-basic-laws.rationale: Keep one essential XOR relationship card and the truth table; remove the separate bare-XOR card that repeated them. Two reference law cards collect notation while the visible behaviour table supports the conditional-inversion question without opening either.

questionsRewritten.logic-boolean-algebra-q11: Replace identity selection and derivation with prediction of conditional inversion.

logic-algebra-demorgan.rationale: Distributivity, absorption-related equivalence and De Morgan transformations earn visible notation because rewriting circuits is the objective. Questions challenge preserved behaviour and the zero boundary of a Python guard rather than memorised algebra.

questionsRewritten.logic-boolean-algebra-q1: Replace algebraic simplification recall with redundant-branch diagnosis.
questionsRewritten.logic-boolean-algebra-q2: Replace symbol manipulation with a practical complemented-condition prediction.
questionsRewritten.logic-boolean-algebra-q6: Replace formula-list recall with behavioural equivalence checks.
questionsRewritten.logic-boolean-algebra-q8: Replace repeated formula substitutions with a direct reasoning walkthrough; preserve the tested behaviour.

logic-algebra-proof.rationale: Majority before/after and consensus equations make the simplification visible; intermediate manipulations are redundant. Runnable exhaustive checks remain, and questions diagnose truth-table coverage and the difference between Python Boolean and integer NOT.

questionsRewritten.logic-boolean-algebra-q4: Clarify Python integer wording so its glossary link does not open the C int type; preserve the independently executed NOT result.
questionsRewritten.logic-boolean-algebra-q5: Replace multi-line algebra with truth-table interpretation.
questionsRewritten.logic-boolean-algebra-q9: Replace consensus formula recall with coverage reasoning while keeping timing caveat.

logic-canonical-minterms.rationale: The row-selecting minterm and canonical SOP notation are essential to learning the representation. Binary row order and each input condition are visible; the question tests why all inputs must be checked rather than converting an index arithmetically.

questionsRewritten.logic-boolean-algebra-q3: Remove binary-index conversion and test the row-selecting mechanism.

logic-maxterms-functions.rationale: Maxterm and POS representations stay visible to show rejection of zero rows. Remove exponential counting formulas: the LUT explanation and questions instead establish independently programmable output rows.

questionsRewritten.logic-boolean-algebra-q7: Replace notation conversion with explanation of the complementary row sets.
questionsRewritten.logic-boolean-algebra-q10: Replace exponential function-count arithmetic with LUT programming behaviour.

logic-universal-gates.rationale: NAND constructions and the two-level NAND network remain essential examples of universality. Gate truth tables and a short netlist are the mechanism, and questions trace gates or derive completeness rather than repeat substitutions.

questionsRewritten.logic-gates-cmos-q2: Replace repeated formula substitutions with a direct reasoning walkthrough; preserve the tested behaviour.
questionsRewritten.logic-gates-cmos-q5: Replace repeated formula substitutions with a direct reasoning walkthrough; preserve the tested behaviour.
questionsRewritten.logic-gates-cmos-q6: Replace nested Boolean derivation with gate-by-gate prediction.
questionsRewritten.logic-gates-cmos-q11: Replace repeated formula substitutions with a direct reasoning walkthrough; preserve the tested behaviour.

logic-cmos-networks.rationale: No formula card is necessary: transistor diagrams and switching conditions explain complementary networks. Questions test which network conducts and the stated construction/sizing assumptions; electrical and library limitations remain visible.

questionsRewritten.logic-gates-cmos-q4: Replace transistor-count arithmetic with polarity and implementation-cost reasoning.

logic-gate-delay-power.rationale: Only the dynamic-power model survives as reference; the visible prose already explains activity, capacitance, squared voltage and frequency effects. Timing and power questions diagnose dependent paths and model scope without arithmetic.

questionsRewritten.logic-gates-cmos-q8: Replace ratio arithmetic with mechanism and model-limit reasoning.
questionsRewritten.logic-gates-cmos-q12: Replace gate-level capacity arithmetic with critical-path diagnosis.

logic-shared-bus-safety.rationale: Unchanged prose and driver-state table already teach contention, idle levels and physical enable delays directly. No formula is useful, and the unchanged question tests electrical contention rather than treating a wire as Boolean OR.

logic-kmap-layout.rationale: Gray-order diagrams and grouping rules explain adjacency and fixed inputs without cell-count equations. Questions check wrap-around, valid rectangles and which variables survive, with all necessary labels visible.

questionsRewritten.logic-karnaugh-maps-q1: Replace repeated formula substitutions with a direct reasoning walkthrough; preserve the tested behaviour.
questionsRewritten.logic-karnaugh-maps-q2: Replace group-size arithmetic with the meaning of eliminating variables.

logic-kmap-worked.rationale: The two final minimised expressions remain essential links from groups to circuit terms; repeated substitutions and smaller equivalent expressions are removed. Questions test irrelevant inputs, corner wrapping and missed required coverage.

questionsRewritten.logic-karnaugh-maps-q3: Replace minterm-symbol manipulation with identifying irrelevant inputs.
questionsRewritten.logic-karnaugh-maps-q4: Replace long alternative expressions with spatial wrap-around reasoning.
questionsRewritten.logic-karnaugh-maps-q5: Replace expression selection with diagnosing incomplete coverage.

logic-kmap-primes.rationale: The essential cover and two alternative minimum covers show the difference between prime and essential groups and non-unique solutions. Independent cube enumeration confirms minimum sizes; questions use coverage witnesses rather than minimisation arithmetic.

questionsRewritten.logic-karnaugh-maps-q9: Replace lengthy minimisation expressions with prime-versus-essential reasoning.
questionsRewritten.logic-karnaugh-maps-q11: Replace counting essential primes with the diagnostic criterion.

logic-kmap-dontcare-pos.rationale: The simplified BCD detector and POS/SOP equivalence remain essential; the stricter detector is a useful optional comparison. The input guarantee and reversed zero-group polarity stay visible, and questions diagnose violations of the interface promise.

questionsRewritten.logic-karnaugh-maps-q6: Replace minimisation formula selection with don't-care contract reasoning.
questionsRewritten.logic-karnaugh-maps-q8: Replace full POS derivation with the reason for reversed polarity in zero groups.
questionsRewritten.logic-karnaugh-maps-q12: Remove repeated strict-versus-don't-care equations; test the interface assumption.

logic-kmap-hazards.rationale: The original and bridged equations remain essential because settled equivalence alone cannot explain the physical glitch. Timing trace and single-input/two-level limits stay visible, and the question identifies the stable bridging condition.

questionsRewritten.logic-karnaugh-maps-q10: Replace formula derivation with physical hazard diagnosis and scope.

logic-mux-decoder.rationale: The two-way mux equation remains essential to connect select polarity to gated paths; selector-count arithmetic is removed. Decoder/mux tables and remaining-variable decomposition support both questions with optional content closed.

entry.definition: A status flag whose meaning depends on the instruction and architecture. After flag-setting addition it reports unsigned carry out; after subtraction Arm reports no borrow while x86 CF reports borrow. Some shifts and other instructions use or preserve it differently.

A status flag whose meaning depends on the instruction and architecture. After flag-setting addition it reports unsigned carry out; after flag-setting subtraction x86 CF reports borrow while Arm C reports no borrow. Other instructions may preserve the flag or use it differently.
